captive_summary: Cancelled-and-never-built proposal — screened, not deep-researched. Hanas LNG Investment (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. signed an investment agreement with the Wanshan District (Zhuhai) government in July 2014 for a 6 mtpa reserve base on Huangmao Island (3 mtpa Phase 1), but the project never advanced past that signing — no construction, no design/EIA publication, no further news since 2014. GEM's own status (cancelled, inferred) matches: nothing was ever built, so there is no as-designed or as-built captive-power question to answer.
confirmed_how: Hanas Group's own press release on the 2014 signing (verified PASS on '黄茅岛'/'珠海') is the only substantive public record of this project; no subsequent filing, construction report, or EIA exists. Independent trade-press coverage (Statista's cancelled-China-LNG-terminals ranking) lists it among China's largest cancelled LNG projects at 6 mtpa, corroborating that it never proceeded to construction.

verification_log.note: Hanas Group's own 2014 press release confirming the signing and location on Huangmao Island, Zhuhai.

Not acted on; flagging only in case a future Discovery/dormant-revival pass wants to re-check Hanas's Guangdong plans.

fuel_basis: Backup/abnormal-condition generation at the site is diesel-fuelled (柴油发电机 = 'diesel generator'), per the project's own environmental impact filing — no gas turbine or gas-fired generator of any kind is named anywhere in that filing.
captive_summary: No on-site gas-fired power generation is documented. The Phase 1 project's official environmental-impact supplement (MEE-published, dated April 2013, covering the receiving-terminal engineering) lists the facility's abnormal-condition emission sources as pigging operations, maintenance, diesel generator (柴油发电机) operation, and emergency venting — a diesel genset for backup, not gas. No gas turbine, gas engine, or captive gas power plant is mentioned anywhere in the filing. The surrounding Gaolan Port Economic Development Zone (chemical/petrochemical park where the terminal sits) is described in the zone's own industrial planning document as served by seven substations with dual-circuit (双回路) grid supply guaranteeing continuous production power, consistent with a grid-fed facility.
confirmed_how: MEE-hosted environmental impact supplement report ('广东珠海LNG项目一期工程接收站工程环境影响补充报告书简本', April 2013, filed by 广东珠海金湾液化天然气有限公司 — the terminal's own operating company) states: '非正常工况下，废气污染源主要来自于清管作业、检修、柴油发电机工作、事故状态下的放空气体' ('Under abnormal operating conditions, exhaust pollution sources mainly come from pigging operations, maintenance, diesel generator operation, and venting during accident conditions') — verified PASS on token '柴油发电机'. Separately, the Zhuhai Economic and Technological Development Zone's chemical-park industrial planning document (《珠海经济技术开发区化工园区产业规划》, Aug 2023) states the zone has seven substations with 双回路供电 (dual-circuit power supply) to guarantee continuous production/domestic power — verified PASS on '双回路供电'. Neither document names any gas turbine, gas engine, or gas-fired generator at the terminal.

verification_log.note: MEE-hosted EIA supplement for the terminal's Phase 1 receiving-station engineering; names only a diesel generator for backup/abnormal-condition power.
Zhuhai chemical-park industrial planning document; describes zone-wide dual-circuit grid supply, consistent with grid-fed operation for facilities in the park including this terminal.

Not to be confused with 'Zhuhai Huangmaodao LNG Terminal' (Hanas-proposed, cancelled) in the same shard, which shares the city name but is an unrelated, unbuilt project.
